clue.text: Running pub is a vocation? He won't say anything different

indicators.note: running here means operating or managing, but as a signal it says the letters of the following words are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: A question whether managing a pub could count as a calling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' reads as managing the pub, but it signals the rearranging of all the letters of PUB IS A VOCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: This mock title is given to someone who only ever states what everybody already knows, never offering a fresh point.

clue.text: Accommodating grievance I moved up slightly

indicators.note: says the letter named just before shifts a little earlier in the word, by one place in this down light

parts.note: a grievance is a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone describing how they brought a grievance a little higher to keep a person happy.
explanation.walkthrough: In COMPLAINT the I swaps one place earlier, ahead of the A: in a down answer, earlier means higher up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accommodating is obliging and willing to go along with others' wishes.

clue.text: Dropping off gear (why at number 2?)

parts.note: nightwear for nodding off; the bracket asks why the British spelling has Y, sounding like 'why', as its second letter where the American form has A

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some equipment being delivered or shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' is falling asleep, not unloading. The American spelling PAJAMAS has A second; the British spelling puts a Y there.
explanation.definitionFit: Night clothes are the outfit people wear to go to sleep, which is what dropping off means.

clue.text: American chaperone I'd not led astray? It won't make much difference

indicators.note: something led astray is taken off its proper course, so these letters wander into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An American chaperone who wonders whether failing to steer someone wrong will matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an amount so tiny relative to what is needed that its effect is negligible.

clue.text: It regularly falls close to town

parts.note: nigh means near or close
T is an abbreviation for town, as on maps

explanation.surface: Something that keeps tumbling down near a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Darkness is said to fall every evening, a daily recurrence.

clue.text: See 1
'Away' frequently — regret not going straight

parts.note: out means away, as in 'she is out'
oft is an old word for often
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone often away, regretting that they have not gone straight, like a reformed criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something bent or misaligned, deviating from the correct line.

clue.text: Fellows can upset Sue breaking moral code 9's predecessor admired

parts.note: Victor and Ian are two men's names, so two fellows

indicators.note: in a down light upset turns the word upside down, so it is read from the bottom up

parts.note: can is slang for a toilet, as is lav

indicators.note: breaking breaks the name apart and resets its letters

explanation.surface: A puzzling scene of men upsetting a can while Sue breaks a code admired by a former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is MAJOR: John Major's predecessor as Prime Minister, Margaret Thatcher, praised this moral code. 'Upset' turns LAV into VAL; 'breaking' rearranges SUE as UES.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatcher championed the nineteenth-century virtues of thrift, self-reliance and family duty under exactly this label.

clue.text: Think about a latte to start with — that's milky

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for think goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to opine is to think or hold a view

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: A suggestion to consider a latte first, since it is milky.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaline describes a milky, translucent white like opal glass.

clue.text: Unstressed syllable was tricky, children admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece is placed inside the other
tricky suggests something twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a difficult syllable that children were let into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' and 'admitted' read as describing the children's struggle, but they are the anagram and container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: The schwa is the neutral vowel sound heard in unstressed syllables, like the first vowel of 'about'.

clue.text: Play two pieces of music covered by singer — earlier spot rejected

indicators.note: earlier places this reversed piece in front of the rest
rejected means thrown back, so the word for spot is read in reverse

parts.note: a spot is a jam, a tight situation

indicators.note: covered by means enclosed, so the singer's name goes round the music pieces

parts.note: Rita Ora is a British pop singer

indicators.note: two means the music piece is used twice in a row

parts.note: a bar is a short measure of music

explanation.surface: A singer covering two tunes, with an earlier performance slot turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' reverses the spot word and 'earlier' puts it in front. Rita Ora is a British pop singer; the answer is Shaw's drama about a Salvation Army officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a George Bernard Shaw stage drama first performed in 1905.

clue.text: Good! An investigator spots what those without tickets may do

definitions.text: what those without tickets may do

parts.note: tec is short for detective
a rash is an outbreak of spots

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight as a detective notices fans without tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: To get into a party or event uninvited, as people lacking admission passes might try.

clue.text: I say, Farage's on fire outside — hide in here!

indicators.note: says one word sits round the others

parts.note: lit means alight, on fire
Nigel Farage was an MEP, a Member of the European Parliament; 'say' marks him as an example

explanation.surface: A panicked cry that a politician is burning outside, so take cover!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb urging concealment, but it is an animal skin: tanners soak hides in this pit. It also hints at bodies hidden in lime.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanners steep animal skins in a pit of lime to loosen the hair, so a skin goes in there.

clue.text: Keys found here after fair old kerfuffle

indicators.note: a kerfuffle is a commotion or fuss, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone finding their keys after a fuss at an old fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keys' are not door keys but islands, the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florida Keys are a chain of small coral islands off the southern tip of this US state.

clue.text: Take issue with apprentice's first firing

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word before it, and places it at the front

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to an apprentice being the first to lose their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take issue' reads as a phrase meaning dispute, but splits into R (take) and SON (issue).
explanation.definitionFit: Firing a building deliberately is the crime of setting it alight.

clue.text: Son on Tyneside gets deceptively spacious accommodation without delay

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the time machine surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the TARDIS is Doctor Who's time machine, bigger inside than out

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the letter for son follows

parts.note: NE stands for north-east, the region of England containing Tyneside

explanation.surface: A Geordie son lands a roomy home without any wait, like an estate agent's boast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without delay' looks like one phrase, but 'without' means outside and 'delay' alone is the definition. Tyneside is Newcastle's area of northeast England.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness or slowness in arriving is the state of being delayed.

clue.text: Dead through drink — see one's leader keel over (is it poisonous?)

indicators.note: through means passing within, so the letter for dead sits inside

parts.note: to toast is to drink to someone

indicators.note: keel over means topple, so in this down light the pieces are turned upside down

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone dead drunk is told to watch a man collapse, wondering about poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keel over' turns LO + O into OOL.
explanation.definitionFit: This fungus is popularly thought of as the poisonous kind of mushroom.

clue.text: Van went fast to catch a flightless bird

indicators.note: catch means trap inside, so the word for went fast surrounds the rest

parts.note: sped means went fast
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: A van speeding along to capture an escaped ostrich-like bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' is not a vehicle but short for vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The van, or vanguard, is the leading part of an advance, like the tip leading an attack.

clue.text: Briefly contact university in charity foundation

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the charity's name

parts.note: Toc H is a Christian charity founded in the First World War
a base is a foundation

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a university about setting up a charitable foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to check in quickly with someone, a brief catch-up.

clue.text: Decipher letter about musician

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the Greek letter's name is read backwards

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Maurice Ravel was a French composer

explanation.surface: Working out a letter written about a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To unravel a mystery is to work it out or solve it.

clue.text: Lack of Tory turn-out is excellent

parts.note: no means none, a lack of

indicators.note: out says the letter for turn is removed

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservative or Tory party
U stands for turn, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: A low Conservative voter turnout is welcomed as a fine result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn-out' looks like voter numbers, but splits: the letter for turn (from U-turn) goes 'out' of the Tory colour. Blue is the British Conservatives' colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble can mean of fine, superior quality, as in a noble wine.

clue.text: See 9
Strange wretch is holding out for the most part

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person, a wretch

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other
most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: A miserable person is holding out, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious can mean odd or peculiar, as in a curious incident.

clue.text: Entertainer's huge ass finally gone

indicators.note: gone says the picked letter is removed

parts.note: cosmic means vast, huge

indicators.note: takes the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A performer whose enormous backside has finally vanished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertainer's' reads as possessive but is 'entertainer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian is a performer whose job is making audiences laugh.

clue.text: Sixth wife in series is fighter

indicators.note: in places the wife's name inside

parts.note: Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's sixth wife

explanation.surface: A sixth wife in a TV series turns out to be a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparrer is a boxer who practises against a partner, a fighter.

clue.text: Queen involved in con? Get outta here!

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the letter for queen goes within

parts.note: a scam is a con, a swindle
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The queen accused of being part of a fraud, with a cry of disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get outta here!' sounds like disbelief but is meant literally: go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Scram is a slangy order telling someone to leave at once.

clue.text: Give Romeo makeover! Trainspotting enthusiast perhaps?

indicators.note: a makeover remodels something, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to give Romeo a new look, wondering if he fancies trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trainspotting' is not the railway hobby but the 1996 film, so a fan of it is a film-goer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan of the film Trainspotting is a cinema enthusiast, one example of a film fan.

clue.text: Tradition for one retiring to country

parts.note: the USA is a country

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: eg means for example, for one

explanation.surface: A custom of someone withdrawing to the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means established custom or practice, as with a convention.

clue.text: Assault on old Liberal leader — court names suspect

indicators.note: an assault on something batters it, so these letters are knocked into a new order
takes the opening letter of the party name

explanation.surface: A former Liberal party chief has been attacked, and a court names a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is OLD, L (Liberal's leader) and COURT NAMES. The answer is a murder suspect in the board game Cluedo.
explanation.definitionFit: This character is one of the six possible culprits in the murder-mystery board game Cluedo.

clue.text: See 24
